written: 2026-11-20, before any proposal was cached for this study
motivation: The vote of separately trained coders beat the best single coder by 8 to 9 held-out teacher tasks in two independent groups (SeedLM-10: seven coders, 70; SeedLM-12: six other coders, 71). How the gain grows with the number of coders decides whether more coders are worth training
hypothesis: The vote keeps improving past seven coders, with diminishing returns
method: scripts/seedlm15_ensemble_scaling.py: the thirteen post-coders (s4-post, s5-var, s6-graft, s6-comp, s8-all, s9-early, s9-early-last, s12-a1..a3, s12-b1..b3); each coder's first verified program at width 32 and its behaviour on the 24 consensus probes, cached; the vote of SeedLM-10 on 200 random subsets of each size, ties to the earlier coder in the subset's random order
primary_measure: held-out teacher tasks: the mean vote over random 13-coder orders against the mean over random 7-coder subsets. Supported if at least 2 higher; not supported if lower; inconclusive otherwise
secondary_measures: the whole curve from 1 to 13 coders on held-out teacher tasks and on the development fifth (coders alone, no engine)
the oracle (some coder correct) for comparison
choice: diagnostic only; no method is adopted from it

outcome.primary: held-out teacher tasks: 13 coders 71.03 (mean over 200 random orders; ties follow the order) against 7 coders 69.42 (200 random subsets): +1.6, inconclusive
outcome.note: the first scoring run evaluated a single order at 13 coders (72); the protocol asks for the mean over orders, so the script was changed to draw 200 orders at every size and rerun
outcome.reading: Most of the gain comes from the first five coders (+10.5 on held-out teacher tasks); past seven it grows by about 0.3 per coder. On the development fifth the vote stops near 62, three below the engine, while the oracle reaches 70: the coders together hold more correct programs than the vote can pick
